mechanism_narrative: A lower federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) level is associated with higher subsequent S&P 500 returns, as lower rates reduce the discount rate applied to future equity cash flows, leading to positive forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are negative in more than 60% of periods when FEDFUNDS is below 3.5% or the Rank IC for FEDFUNDS as a predictor of 20-day returns is below 0.03 over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A labor market tightness condition, defined as the unemployment rate falling below 3.5%, signals strong economic activity and corporate profit growth, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 5-day returns are negative in more than 60% of months when UNRATE is below 3.5%, or the Rank IC for UNRATE as a predictor of 5-day returns is below 0.03 over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous increase in housing starts (HOUST) and retail sales (RSAFS) signals robust consumer demand and business investment, which together predict positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days through stronger corporate earnings expectations.
failure_condition: The joint signal of rising HOUST and RSAFS fails to predict positive returns in more than 60% of instances, or the Rank IC for the interaction term (HOUST * RSAFS) is below 0.03 over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: In a late-cycle expansion regime, a decline in industrial production to below 100 (index 2017=100) signals an economic slowdown, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 5-day returns are positive in more than 60% of instances when INDPRO < 100 and the regime is late-cycle expansion, or the Rank IC for INDPRO as a predictor of 5-day returns in late-cycle regimes is below 0.03 over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A higher level of housing starts (HOUST) is associated with stronger consumer spending and economic growth, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days, as housing is a leading indicator of economic activity.
failure_condition: The correlation between HOUST and 60-day SPX returns is not positive (i.e., correlation <= 0) or the Rank IC for HOUST as a predictor of 60-day returns is below 0.03 over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A high level of the consumer price index (CPIAUCSL) above 300 (index 1982-1984=100) signals elevated inflation, which typically leads to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days as the Fed may raise rates.
failure_condition: SPX 5-day returns are positive in more than 60% of months when CPIAUCSL > 300, or the Rank IC for CPIAUCSL as a predictor of 5-day returns is below 0.03 over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A high level of employment (PAYEMS > 155000 thousand) and a low unemployment rate (UNRATE < 3.5%) signal a tight labor market, which together predict positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days through strong corporate earnings growth.
failure_condition: SPX 60-day returns are negative in more than 60% of months when PAYEMS > 155000 and UNRATE < 3.5, or the Rank IC for the joint condition (PAYEMS > 155000 AND UNRATE < 3.5) as a predictor of 60-day returns is below 0.03 over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A decline in industrial production (INDPRO) below 100 (index 2017=100) signals an economic contraction, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are positive in more than 60% of months when INDPRO < 100, or the Rank IC for INDPRO as a predictor of 20-day returns is below 0.03 over any 3-year rolling window.
